I’ve always been a bit of a worrier, but for about the past year it’s like my brain never shuts off. From the moment I wake up, I’m running through everything that could go wrong at the restaurant—food costs, bad reviews, someone getting sick, the oven breaking—and then it spirals into money, my marriage, my health, even if I locked the door. My wife was furious—it was impulsive, and it put us in a hole—but in the moment it felt like if I didn’t act right then, all my worries would come true.

At home I’m exhausted but can’t fall asleep; I just lie there replaying every possible disaster. I used to be proud of my specials, my reviews, but lately I catch myself thinking, “Who cares?” even when something goes well.
